The treatment atlas

Types of cancer treatment.
Different tools, different targets.

A treatment plan is built from multiple clues: cancer type, stage, biomarkers, overall health, previous treatments, and the goals of care. Many people receive more than one type of treatment.

00Archive index01Cancer types02Genes & biomarkers03Diagnosis04Treatment05Awareness
IN THIS FILEHow plans are builtLocal treatmentSystemic treatmentPrecision approachesTrusted sources

There is no single cancer treatment because cancer is not one disease. The same treatment can play different roles depending on the diagnosis and goal.

01 / BUILDING A PLAN

Treatment follows the evidence.

Care teams consider where a cancer began, its exact type, how far it extends, molecular features, and a person’s health and preferences. Treatment may aim to remove or destroy cancer, lower the chance of recurrence, slow growth, or relieve symptoms.

IDENTITY

Type & subtype

Defines the disease more precisely than the word “cancer” alone.

EXTENT

Stage

Describes how much cancer is present and where it is located.

MOLECULAR DETAIL

Biomarkers

May reveal features connected to particular treatment choices.

02 / LOCAL APPROACHES

Some treatments focus on one area.

SURGERY

Remove cancer from the body

Most often used for solid tumors in a defined area. Surgery can diagnose, stage, or treat cancer depending on the situation.

RADIATION THERAPY

Direct energy at a target

Uses high doses of radiation to damage cancer cells and shrink tumors. It is often directed at a particular part of the body.

Local treatment can still affect healthy tissue near the target. The expected benefits, risks, and side effects depend on the exact procedure and location.

03 / SYSTEMIC APPROACHES

Other treatments travel through the body.

CHEMOTHERAPY

Act on rapidly dividing cells

Uses drugs to kill cancer cells or slow their growth. It can also affect healthy cells that divide quickly.

IMMUNOTHERAPY

Help the immune system fight cancer

Includes several approaches that change or strengthen parts of the immune response.

HORMONE THERAPY

Block growth signals

Can slow cancers that use certain hormones to grow, including some breast and prostate cancers.

STEM CELL TRANSPLANT

Restore blood-forming cells

Can restore stem cells after very high-dose treatment in certain blood cancers and related conditions.

04 / PRECISION APPROACHES

Some treatments focus on a feature of the cancer.

Targeted therapies act on specific proteins or other changes that help cancer cells grow, divide, or spread. Biomarker testing may be needed to learn whether a target is present.

A detected target does not guarantee that a treatment will work. Cancer cells can also change over time or find another way to grow, which may create treatment resistance.

ONE PLAN MAY USE SEVERAL TOOLS

Surgery, radiation, medicines, and supportive care can be used before, during, or after one another. The order and combination are specific to the person and cancer.
